meta.note: Every study below was opened live via Europe PMC during the run. ABSTRACT-LEVEL access only: full methods tables and VITAL's enrolled 25(OH)D distribution were not read. Deficiency-correction and osteomalacia rows rest on guideline consensus, not on a treatment RCT opened this run. Not yet human-verified.

product: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) 2000 IU (50 mcg) per day, taken alone
dose_note: Most fracture benefit in the literature comes from vitamin D PLUS calcium, so it does not transfer to this product used by itself.

for_whom.reasonable: If you are deficient, over 75, pregnant, or a child/teen — mainly to fix or prevent a shortfall.
for_whom.not_shown: If you are a healthy adult under 75 with normal levels, no benefit has been shown for bones, falls, colds, mood or lifespan.
for_whom.source: Endocrine Society 2024 guideline (PMID 38828931) suggests against supplementing above the DRI in healthy adults under 75.

outcomes.name: Fixing a low level
outcomes.sentence: Taking it reliably raises a low blood level — that is the thing it definitely does. It is a blood marker, not yet a health outcome.

ledger.effect_basis: D2d RCT: 25(OH)D rose 27.7 to 54.3 ng/mL on daily D3; surrogate endpoint

effect.found: Daily D3 raises 25(OH)D dependably; the lower you start, the bigger the rise.
effect.missing: This is the blood number, not a symptom or an event you feel.
effect.move: Trials showing the corrected level changes how people actually do.

evidence.missing: Only one trial's response curve was read in full this run.

form.found: Plain oral D3, exactly this form.

dose.found: 2000 IU is a standard corrective dose.

inventory.note: D2d: 25(OH)D 27.7 to 54.3 ng/mL on 4000 IU daily

outcomes.strongest_study: D2d (Pittas 2019) — measured blood-level response inside a randomised trial
outcomes.strongest_doubt: It is a surrogate: correcting the number did not deliver the downstream benefits in the same trials
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: A trial showing corrected levels change symptoms or events in deficient people

outcomes.name: Bones · fractures
outcomes.population: community adults under 75, normal levels, no calcium
outcomes.sentence: 25,871 adults, this exact dose, 5.3 years: no fewer fractures (HR 0.98). Newer pooled data agree, with high certainty.

ledger.effect_basis: VITAL HR 0.98 (0.89-1.08); BMJ 2026 MA of 69 trials RR 1.00 (0.95-1.06) high certainty for D alone
ledger.effective_daily_range: none for D alone in this group

effect.found: No reduction in total, non-vertebral or hip fractures.
effect.missing: Nothing — this is a well-shown null, not a gap.
effect.move: Nothing realistic; the question is settled for this group.

evidence.found: One 25,871-person trial at this exact dose plus a high-certainty review of 69 trials.

form.found: Daily oral D3, exactly as sold.

dose.found: 2000 IU is the precise dose tested.

inventory.note: 69 trials; D alone RR 1.00, high certainty; VITAL pooled inside
D alone any fracture RR 1.06, hip 1.14

outcomes.strongest_study: VITAL (LeBoff 2022) at this exact dose in 25,871 adults
outcomes.strongest_doubt: None credible for this population; the positive fracture literature is the calcium-combined, high-risk one
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: Nothing plausible — several large trials already agree

outcomes.name: Bones · with calcium, over 75
outcomes.population: older or care-home adults taking calcium too
outcomes.sentence: Vitamin D plus calcium cuts hip fractures in older high-risk adults (RR 0.84) — but that is a different regimen from this product alone.

ledger.effect_basis: Yao 2019: D+Ca any fracture RR 0.94 (0.89-0.99), hip 0.84 (0.72-0.97); BMJ 2026 combined RR 0.91 but judges absolute gain small

effect.found: About a 16% relative drop in hip fracture — concentrated in care-home residents.
effect.missing: The absolute gain is small; the newest review calls it not clearly meaningful.
effect.move: A trial in high-risk older adults using this dose plus calcium.

evidence.found: Two large pooled analyses agree on direction.

form.found: Requires calcium alongside — this product does not include it.
form.missing: Evidence for D alone in this group.

inventory.note: combined RR 0.91 (0.84-0.99) but small absolute effect

outcomes.strongest_study: Yao 2019 pooled analysis of 49,282 on D plus calcium
outcomes.strongest_doubt: BMJ 2026 judges even the combined benefit below a clinically meaningful threshold
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: A high-risk trial of 2000 IU plus calcium reporting absolute risk

outcomes.name: Colds & flu
outcomes.sentence: 40 trials, 61,589 people: no reliable reduction (OR 0.94, CI touches 1). The older positive result did not survive the bigger analysis.

ledger.effect_basis: Jolliffe 2025 OR 0.94 (0.88-1.00) p=0.057; NO effect modification by baseline 25(OH)D, dose or dosing frequency; funnel asymmetry p=0.002 in the older positive literature

effect.found: No reliable drop in respiratory infections, including in people who start low.
effect.missing: The 2017 analysis suggested big protection in the very deficient — the 2025 update found no such interaction.
effect.move: A large trial dedicated to severely deficient people.

evidence.found: 40 trials, 61,589 people, including the large daily-dose trials.

form.found: Daily oral D3 — the regimen once thought to matter.

dose.found: 2000 IU daily is well inside the tested range.

inventory.note: 40 RCTs OR 0.94 (0.88-1.00); no modification by baseline status; Egger p=0.002
superseded: IPD OR 0.88, deficient subgroup 0.30, p-interaction 0.05

outcomes.strongest_study: Jolliffe 2025 — the largest and newest analysis, and it is null
outcomes.strongest_doubt: Martineau 2017 found strong protection in the very deficient; the newer interaction test contradicts it
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: An RCT enrolling only people below 25 nmol/L with infection as the primary endpoint

outcomes.name: Mood · preventing depression
outcomes.population: adults 50+ who are not currently depressed
outcomes.sentence: 18,353 adults, 5 years, this exact dose: it did not prevent depression and did not shift mood scores (HR 0.97).

ledger.effect_basis: VITAL-DEP HR 0.97; no PHQ-8 change against a stated 0.5-point meaningful difference

effect.found: No prevention of depression, no change in mood scores.
effect.missing: Nothing for this question — it is the definitive prevention trial.

evidence.found: One 18,353-person, 5-year randomised trial at exactly this dose.

inventory.note: VITAL-DEP, 2000 IU, 5.3 y, HR 0.97, MCID 0.5 pts

outcomes.strongest_doubt: It says nothing about people who are already depressed — a separate question, scored separately
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: Nothing for prevention in this group

outcomes.name: Mood · if you are depressed AND low
outcomes.population: people who are currently depressed and deficient
outcomes.sentence: Genuinely unknown. The big trial only tested prevention in healthy people, so it does not answer this.

ledger.effect_basis: no dedicated deficient-and-depressed treatment RCT was opened this run; small meta-analyses exist but were not verified

effect.found: Nothing verified in this run — this is a gap, not a null.
effect.missing: A trial in people who are both depressed and deficient.
effect.move: A placebo-controlled treatment trial in that group.

evidence.found: No source opened for this specific question.

form.found: The form is not in question.

dose.missing: No established treatment dose for this indication.

outcomes.strongest_doubt: Small positive trials here are the type most prone to publication bias
outcomes.study_that_would_move_this: An RCT of D3 in depressed, deficient adults with a depression scale as the primary endpoint

searches_run: Europe PMC: vitamin D fracture meta-analysis baseline deficiency
BMJ 2026 calcium vitamin D fractures falls 69 trials
could_not_access: full texts (abstract-level Europe PMC access only)
NIH ODS and Endocrine Society primary web pages (guideline read via indexed record PMID 38828931)
confidence_note: Nulls for replete adults under 75 are well established by trials at this exact dose. The deficiency-correction and osteomalacia claims rest on guideline consensus rather than a treatment RCT opened this run, and are labelled accordingly.
